newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Loy Yang Power issuing A$300 mln CPI bonds.
newsitem.headline: Loy Yang Power issuing A$300 mln CPI bonds.

text.p: Macquarie Bank and ANZ Investment Bank, as underwriters, said on Tuesday they will begin selling down A$300 million of inflation indexed bonds issued by Loy Yang Power this week to partially finance the A$4.9 billion purchase of Victoria's Loy Yang A power station.
Loy Yang Power is an Australian-based consortium which was selected by the Victorian State government to buy the Loy Yang A Power Station and brown coal mine in Victoria's La Trobe Valley.

The inflation index annuity bonds will be priced at 160 basis points over the benchmark Commonwealth 2010 indexed bond, which at current market levels implies a real yield of about 6.3 percent, plus the rate of inflation.
The bonds, maturing on May 12, 2027, compare favourably with other infrastructure related bonds, which currently trade at 130 basis points over government bonds, the underwriters said.
David Hornery, Head of Securities at ANZ Investment Bank, said the underwriters expect strong institutional demand for securities, based on early expressions of interest.
Australian Mutual Provident Society has taken up A$50 million and the remainder is expected to be keenly sought by superannuation and infrastructure funds, Horney added.

Macquarie Bank Debt Markets Division Head Els Termaat said the bonds are attractive because they are high yielding securities linked to inflation and they are inexpensive compared with other infrastructure bonds currently in the market.
"We also believe there will be a contraction in the yield margin in secondary market trading, providing investors with a capital gain," Termaat said.
She added that the success of the M2 and Melbourne City Link indexed bond issues has left the market comfortable with indexed bonds to fund major infrastructure projects.

"Instututional investors see infrastructure financings like Loy Yang Power as adding value to their funds under management and as such are committed to supporting the market's further development," ANZ Investment Bank's Hornery said.
Loy Yang Power CPI bond holders will bear project risk.
Apart from the CPI bond facility, a project facility for A$2.9 billion senior debt and A$300 million of junior debt has been arranged. Also, A$1.3 billion in equity has been raised.
The Loy Yang consortium is led by U.S. utilities NRG Energy Inc and CMS Energy Corp, and also includes Macquarie Bank Ltd's Infrastructure Trust.
